34bd24381e1c7ef52abe5ac8b4433649d40f0dba.summary: Socket reports that a threat actor used compromised maintainer accounts and the project's own GitHub automation to publish a malicious @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 npm release and a trojanized Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 on November 9, 2026. Both carry a loader that fetches and runs remote JavaScript, reusing SleepyDuck Ethereum-addressed C2 infrastructure that Pluto Security linked to a 2025 campaign. Later stages reportedly install a Go backdoor on macOS and Linux and ScreenConnect remote access on Windows, and target node config and keys. npm removed 13.3.0 after about 75 minutes. 34d1144c2183487f403172e7b3c629fdeeb9688a.summary: Malwarebytes Threat Intelligence describes a late-June malspam campaign it attributes to the FIN7 APT group. The attack drops JSSLoader, a rewrite of the loader with expanded capabilities including data exfiltration, and a secondary .NET payload. The report also notes an earlier XLL-format component of FIN7 that others had described.

342911a43de57cd66a23bf4c1037bb5ee7fe12ab.summary: Entry for the Olympic Destroyer malware family, credited to Fraunhofer FKIE. It describes the malware as seeming to have no function other than to disrupt computer systems related to the 2018 Winter Olympic event. The rest of the text is an index of dated titles, authors and sources of articles about the family, with no analysis of its own, so it is treated as an index rather than a threat report.

345738dbeb92bc8a15082cba3d7f370c123a7f7c.summary: Report on the guilty plea of Andrii Kolpakov, a Ukrainian national that the U.S. prosecutors describe as a manager and recruiter for FIN7, a cybercrime group. The group is said to have stolen more than $1 billion by posing as a penetration-testing vendor. The plea deal sets losses at over $100 million. Spanish police arrested Kolpakov in June 2018 and he was extradited to the U.S. in 2019. He faces up to 25 years in prison. Fedir Hladyr, another FIN7 member, pleaded guilty in September 2019 and is scheduled for sentencing on Dec. 11.
